disposition: bitter orange topical record
assessment: Table 2 identifies bitter orange fruit applied to abscesses and ulcers. The survey gives no whole sweet orange or measured constipation outcome.

disposition: bilberry fruit ethnobotany
assessment: Vaccinium myrtillus fruit was used in jam and reportedly for intestinal function; decoction was described for diarrhea. No clinical study, diagnosed Parkinson cohort or specified blueberry preparation was assigned.

disposition: blackberry jam and sore throat use
assessment: Rubus ulmifolius fruit jam was recalled for sore throat. Separate leaf, root and aerial preparations were reported. The survey gives no frozen fruit pain rating or clinical intervention.

disposition: cherry used for food and other traditional indications
assessment: Prunus avium fruit is reported as nutrient-rich and laxative in large quantities. Cherry stalk and seed uses differ. None reports measured fatigue after cherry fruit or a Parkinson cohort.

disposition: grape must, wine and vinegar in reported uses
assessment: Table 2 lists grape must in food and wine and vinegar as distinct preparations. It gives no measurement of anxiety after consuming grapes.

disposition: wild carrot root and different intestinal symptom
assessment: Daucus carota roots were recalled as a remedy for diarrhea and leafy or flower preparations for other uses. Constipation severity was not measured.

disposition: potato and other customary uses
assessment: The Solanum tuberosum entry records traditional uses without a potato-insomnia observation. Insomnia remedies elsewhere in the table concern distinct plants.

disposition: cauliflower listed without anxiety assessment
assessment: Brassica oleracea is listed as cauliflower. The survey does not connect eating it to a measured anxiety outcome.

disposition: wild asparagus and different reported indications
assessment: The Asparagus acutifolius record gives diuretic, digestive and rheumatic uses. The survey measures citation frequencies and has no asparagus fatigue score.

disposition: oat preparational uses and unmatched sleep indication
assessment: Oat fruit was referenced as food and its decoction for restorative, laxative and calming uses. Sleep claims elsewhere do not estimate an oat-insomnia result.

disposition: barley coffee substitute and topical or digestive uses
assessment: The article describes roasted barley as a coffee substitute and different preparations for the throat and digestive uses. No barley anxiety outcome was measured.

disposition: chickens in husbandry or veterinary uses
assessment: Chicken occurrences include farm feed and veterinary uses of ash bark. The report does not measure fatigue following chicken consumed as food.

disposition: coffee and other roasted beverages
assessment: Coffea arabica seeds are recalled for halitosis, and other taxa are listed as wartime beverage substitutes. No brewed coffee fatigue rating was measured, so this archive match does not affect the clinical assessment.

disposition: basil in ethnobotanical reports of other uses
assessment: Basil leaf preparations were reported for digestive uses, vomiting, anxiety, and oral inflammation. These reports provide no named fatigue, constipation or insomnia endpoint.

disposition: parsley in intestinal-gas remedy
assessment: Parsley was included in a mixed fennel, celery and butcher's broom syrup for intestinal gas. This is not an oral parsley constipation study.

disposition: reported toothache and heart-pain preparations
assessment: Interviewees describe a topical parsley-leaf pulp mixture for toothache and a parsley-stem wine remedy for heart pain. There is no isolated parsley effect or clinical pain score.

disposition: parsley compress and eye tiredness
assessment: Fresh parsley juice was reported in an eye compress for tired eyes. No systemic oral fatigue or Parkinson outcome was measured.

disposition: chive food, diuresis, and separate indications
assessment: The vouchered common chive aerial part is listed as food and in reports of diuresis, intestinal parasites and heartbeat. Constipation and anxiety severity were not measured.

disposition: oregano digestive and topical uses
assessment: Fresh or dried oregano leaf infusion is described for digestion and heartburn. Essential oil is described for other uses. No measured anxiety endpoint.

disposition: marjoram for flavor and other indications
assessment: Fresh or dried marjoram leaf infusion is recorded for cough, cold, digestion and migraine. No measured insomnia outcome.

disposition: thyme in preparations for other symptoms
assessment: Reported thyme uses include digestion, cough and mixed-headache remedies. The survey gives no isolated thyme or Parkinson anxiety contrast.

disposition: rosemary variety of reported uses
assessment: The rosemary row describes leaf or flower preparations for colitis, abdominal discomfort and other uses. It contains no oral rosemary depression or constipation-severity comparison.

disposition: sage preparations and localized pain folk uses
assessment: Informants reported chewing sage leaves for toothache and using decoction for stomach or menstrual pain. This is a use report without prospective symptom measurement, identified freshness or Parkinson pain.

disposition: sage oral uses and different endpoints
assessment: The sage entries describe culinary, digestive, oral and other traditional uses. The tonic reference concerns a wine infusion, and no fatigue score or insomnia effect was measured.

disposition: tarragon use in food and root decoction
assessment: The vouchered tarragon leaf flavors foods and is considered digestive. A root decoction is mentioned for sore throat. The row gives no measured pain, fatigue, insomnia or depressive outcome.

disposition: laurel leaf and different customary uses
assessment: Bay is used as a seasoning and in reports of digestive, intestinal gas and sedative preparations. The record gives no separate constipation or fatigue measurement.

disposition: lemon balm and self-reported traditional mood use
assessment: Dried aerial-part decoction was recalled for unspecified mood changes, and infusion to reduce insomnia. The report gives no depression scale or clinical treatment follow-up.

disposition: Capsicum species and unmatched indication
assessment: The Capsicum annuum entry is called chili and gives no variety, paprika or cayenne-specific exposure. No anxiety or insomnia result was measured.

disposition: uncertain Capsicum type and reported localized pain use
assessment: The chili entry records aerial-part infusion for rheumatic pain and fruit for hemorrhoid pain. It gives neither a paprika or cayenne cultivar-specific result nor a measured Parkinson pain outcome.

disposition: ginger rhizome in cooking and fever infusion
assessment: Zingiber officinale was mentioned for cookery and rhizome infusion for fever. Constipation, pain and anxiety were not assessed after the named exposure.

disposition: caraway common-name collision and food use
assessment: The Italian common name Cumino is attached here to vouchered Carum carvi fruits used in cooking. No fatigue measurement accompanies the record.

disposition: anise in mixed antacid and other uses
assessment: Aniseed, parsley and fennel are recorded together for gastric acidity. Other anise uses concern hiccups, hair or other indications. No assessed pain, fatigue or insomnia severity.

disposition: clove use and unmatched anxiety endpoint
assessment: Clove appears as food, dental use and domestic perfume or repellent. The survey gives no anxiety outcome after eating clove.

disposition: clove placed on an aching tooth
assessment: Clove applied to a tooth and flower infusion used as a mouth rinse were cited for toothache. These are interview reports of topical use rather than a clinical pain score after ground clove.

disposition: saffron pistils as a culinary use
assessment: The saffron row lists cooking use only. It gives no depression, insomnia or fatigue assessment and does not alter the clinical trial evidence.

disposition: traditional oral olive oil for intestinal transit
assessment: Nine hill-area citations described orally taking olive oil to promote intestinal transit. Oil grade and symptom change were not measured, and the interview was not a study of Parkinson constipation.

disposition: olive oil vehicle and mixed herbal uses
assessment: Table 2 records oil as a culinary or topical ingredient and carrier for herbal preparations. Relaxation and insomnia uses are attributed to other preparations, without an oil-specific clinical result.

disposition: walnut fruit and oil distinguished
assessment: Whole walnuts were recalled for stress or migraines. The pressed oil was used for cooking and was believed to lower cholesterol. The survey gives no oil-specific measured pain, anxiety or depression outcome.

disposition: almond oil cited for other uses
assessment: Almond oil recalls concern skin conditions, parasites and muscle relaxation. No study of almond oil and depressive symptoms.

disposition: traditional celery pain and extracted-leaf assay
assessment: The introduction cites whole celery as a customary remedy for rheumatic pain. Experiments measure essential-oil composition and in vitro activity after shade-dried leaf extraction. No pain behavior or clinical assessment was included.
